summary: Unpinned third-party GitHub dependency fetched and executed at install
details: This unofficial fork of Baileys declares a production dependency sourced directly from a GitHub repository with no commit pin: `"libsignal": "github:Cogils/libsignal-node"` in package.json. `npm install` resolves that source off-registry, fetches whatever the branch tip currently holds, and runs any lifecycle scripts inside it. The referenced repository is owned by a third party (`Cogils`), unrelated to the upstream WhiskeySockets/Baileys publisher, so whoever controls that repo controls code executed on the installer's machine at install time. The package also presents low-trust provenance: it is published under `@izi-coder` as an unofficial Baileys fork, the manifest's repository URL points at a Telegram channel rather than a source host, and `lib/index.js` prints a hostile ASCII banner and Telegram self-promo links on import.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
